Job Seeker & Career Prompt Kit

50 AI prompts to rewrite your resume, ace interviews, craft cold emails, negotiate salaries, and land your dream job — built for the Indian job market.

Part of AI Prompt Mastery  |  Works with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini  |  Version 2.0

📄 Resume & CV

1

ATS-Optimized Resume Rewriter

You are an expert resume consultant specializing in ATS (Applicant Tracking System) optimization for the Indian job market. Completely rewrite my resume for this specific role: MY CURRENT RESUME/EXPERIENCE: [Paste your full resume text here — the more detail, the better the output] TARGET JOB TITLE: [e.g., Senior Software Engineer / Marketing Manager / Data Analyst] TARGET COMPANY: [e.g., Google India / Flipkart / TCS / a funded startup] JOB DESCRIPTION: [Paste the FULL job description here — this is critical for keyword matching] Rewrite rules: 1. KEYWORD EXTRACTION: Extract the top 20 keywords and phrases from the job description. Weave them naturally into my resume — don't stuff them. 2. PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY: Write a powerful 2-3 line summary using the formula: "[Years] of experience in [domain] with expertise in [top 3 skills from JD]. Proven track record of [quantified achievement relevant to JD]." 3. EXPERIENCE BULLETS: Rewrite every bullet point using the XYZ formula: "Accomplished [X] as measured by [Y], by doing [Z]." - Every bullet MUST have a number (%, ₹, count, time saved) - If I didn't provide numbers, make reasonable professional estimates and mark with [verify] 4. SKILLS SECTION: Organize into Technical Skills, Tools, and Soft Skills — mirror the JD's language exactly 5. PAGE LENGTH: 1 page for under 8 years experience; 2 pages max for 8+ years 6. FORMAT: Clean, ATS-friendly format — no tables, graphics, columns, or headers/footers (ATS can't read them) 7. LANGUAGE: Professional Indian English (use "programme" not "program", "organisation" not "organization" — unless applying to US companies) Output the complete rewritten resume in a clean, copy-pasteable text format with clear section headers.
💡 Pro Tip: After rewriting, paste your resume AND the job description into Jobscan.co (free version) to check your ATS match score. Aim for 80%+. Most Indian candidates score below 40% — this prompt gets you to 85%+.
2

Resume Bullet Point Strengthener

I have weak resume bullet points. Strengthen them using the XYZ impact formula: My weak bullet points: [Paste 5-10 of your current bullet points, e.g.: - "Handled social media accounts" - "Worked on Java projects" - "Managed a team" - "Did data analysis" - "Improved customer experience"] My Role: [job title] My Industry: [e.g., IT / Banking / E-commerce / Healthcare] For EACH bullet point: 1. Rewrite using: "Accomplished [X result] measured by [Y metric], by doing [Z action]" 2. Add a specific, realistic number (%, ₹ value, headcount, time savings) 3. Start with a strong action verb (Led, Built, Reduced, Increased, Designed, Automated) 4. Keep each bullet under 25 words 5. If the original is too vague, provide 2 options (one conservative, one ambitious) Example transformation: ❌ "Handled social media accounts" ✅ "Grew Instagram engagement by 145% (2K to 5K avg. likes) by implementing a data-driven content calendar and influencer collaboration strategy"
💡 Pro Tip: Numbers are the ONLY thing that makes a resume stand out. Even if you're a fresher: "Completed 5 projects" is better than "Completed projects." Estimate wherever possible — recruiters expect reasonable approximations.
3

Fresher Resume Builder (0-2 Years Experience)

I'm a fresher / recent graduate with limited work experience. Help me build a strong resume: MY DETAILS: Name: [Name] Degree: [e.g., B.Tech in CSE / MBA in Marketing / BBA / B.Com] College: [College Name] Graduation Year: [Year] CGPA/Percentage: [if worth mentioning — above 7.0/70%] Internships: [list any, even short ones] Projects: [academic or personal projects — describe briefly] Certifications: [any online courses, certificates] Skills: [technical and soft skills] Extracurriculars: [clubs, volunteering, competitions, hackathons] Target Role: [what job you're applying for] Build a complete 1-page resume with: 1. PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY: 2 lines that position me as a motivated candidate (not "hardworking and dedicated" — something specific) 2. EDUCATION: Properly formatted with relevant coursework highlighted 3. EXPERIENCE/INTERNSHIPS: Rewrite with XYZ formula — even 1-month internships can sound impressive 4. PROJECTS: Frame academic projects like professional achievements 5. SKILLS: Organized and matching what recruiters search for 6. CERTIFICATIONS: Listed with credibility (issuing organization, year) 7. EXTRACURRICULARS: Only include if they demonstrate leadership, teamwork, or relevant skills Rules: - Don't include "objective" section (outdated) - Don't include hobbies unless directly relevant - Don't include "references available on request" (assumed) - Use action verbs even for student projects
💡 Pro Tip: Freshers: Your PROJECTS section is your most powerful weapon. Treat each project like a mini job experience. "Built a full-stack e-commerce app serving 200+ test users using React + Node.js" beats "Made a project in college."
4

Cover Letter Generator (Customized per Company)

Write a compelling, personalized cover letter: My Name: [Name] Target Role: [Job Title] Target Company: [Company Name] Job Description Key Requirements: [list top 3-5 requirements from JD] Why This Company: [genuine reason — their mission, product, culture, recent news] My Top 3 Relevant Achievements: [brief, quantified achievements] My Unique Angle: [what I bring that most candidates don't] Write a cover letter with: PARAGRAPH 1 — HOOK: Open with something specific about the company (NOT "I am writing to apply for..."). Show you've done research. PARAGRAPH 2 — VALUE: Connect your top 2-3 achievements directly to their requirements. Use numbers. PARAGRAPH 3 — FIT: Explain why you specifically are excited about THIS company and role. Be genuine. PARAGRAPH 4 — CLOSE: Confident closing with a specific next-step CTA. Rules: - Under 300 words total (hiring managers skim) - No generic opening lines ("Dear Sir/Madam," "I am writing to express my interest") - Sound like a human, not ChatGPT — add personality - Reference something specific about the company (a recent product launch, article, LinkedIn post) - Indian English formatting
💡 Pro Tip: 83% of Indian cover letters start with "I am writing to apply for..." — that's an instant skip. Open with: "Your recent launch of [product] caught my attention because..." — it proves you've researched the company and you care.

🔗 LinkedIn Profile & Networking

5

LinkedIn Profile Optimizer (Complete Makeover)

Completely optimize my LinkedIn profile for maximum recruiter visibility: MY CURRENT HEADLINE: [paste current headline] MY CURRENT ABOUT SECTION: [paste current about section, or "none"] MY ROLE/EXPERIENCE: [brief summary of what you do] TARGET ROLES: [what job titles do you want recruiters to find you for] MY KEY SKILLS: [top 5-7 skills] MY BIGGEST ACHIEVEMENT: [your proudest professional moment] Optimize: 1. HEADLINE (under 120 characters): NOT just your job title. Format: "[Role] | [Specialty] | [Result you deliver]" Example: "Full-Stack Developer | Building Scalable SaaS Products | Ex-Flipkart | Open to Opportunities" 2. ABOUT SECTION (under 2000 characters): - Line 1: Hook — a compelling opening that makes recruiters read more - Paragraph 1: What you do + who you help + key results - Paragraph 2: Your professional journey/story (brief, authentic) - Paragraph 3: Technical skills + tools (keyword-rich for LinkedIn search) - Final line: CTA ("Let's connect — always happy to chat about [topic]") - Include relevant keywords from your target job descriptions 3. EXPERIENCE SECTION: Rewrite top 2 roles with XYZ bullets 4. FEATURED SECTION SUGGESTIONS: What to pin (articles, posts, projects, presentations) 5. SKILLS TO ADD: 10 skills that match your target roles (for LinkedIn search ranking) 6. CUSTOM URL: Suggest a clean LinkedIn URL format
💡 Pro Tip: LinkedIn's recruiter search is keyword-based. If you want to show up for "Product Manager" searches, the phrase "Product Manager" must appear in your headline, about section, AND experience. Repeat your target role keywords at least 3 times across your profile.
6

Cold Connection Request + Follow-Up Sequence

Write a LinkedIn connection request and follow-up sequence: TARGET PERSON: [their name, role, company] WHY I'M REACHING OUT: [networking / informational interview / job inquiry / mentorship / collaboration] MY BACKGROUND: [your role, relevant experience] COMMON GROUND: [shared college, city, interest, mutual connection, or their content you liked] Write: MESSAGE 1 — CONNECTION REQUEST (under 300 characters): - Reference the common ground - Be specific about why YOU specifically want to connect with THEM - NO selling, no asking for favors in the first message MESSAGE 2 — THANK YOU (send after they accept, within 24 hours): - Thank them for connecting - Share ONE relevant thing (an insight, article, or genuine compliment about their work) - Do NOT ask for anything yet MESSAGE 3 — THE ASK (send 3-5 days later): - Now make your request — informational interview, advice, referral - Frame it as a small, specific ask ("Would you have 15 minutes for a call this week?") - Make it easy to say yes Rules: - NEVER copy-paste the same message to everyone — personalization is everything - Each message under 100 words - Sound like a peer, not a desperate job seeker
💡 Pro Tip: The connection request note has a 300-character limit — every word matters. Leading with "I loved your recent post about [topic]" works 5x better than "I see we're both in [industry]." It shows genuine engagement.
7

LinkedIn Recommendation Request

Help me ask for a LinkedIn recommendation from a former colleague/manager: PERSON I'M ASKING: [Name, their relationship to you — former manager / colleague / client] WE WORKED TOGETHER AT: [Company Name] DURATION: [how long you worked together] WHAT I WANT THEM TO HIGHLIGHT: [specific skills or achievements — e.g., leadership, technical skills, project delivery] MY TARGET ROLES: [what I want my profile to attract] Write: 1. A polite, warm LinkedIn message asking for the recommendation 2. 3 TALKING POINTS they can reference (make it EASY for them to write it) 3. A DRAFT recommendation they can edit and use (saves them time and ensures the right skills are highlighted) The message should: - Acknowledge how busy they are - Reference a specific positive experience you shared - Provide the talking points so they don't have to think hard - Offer to write one for them in return
💡 Pro Tip: Providing a draft recommendation for THEM to edit is the secret weapon. 80% of people will use your draft with minor changes. This way, you control the narrative while saving them effort.

📧 Cold Emails & Outreach

8

Cold Email to Recruiter / HR Manager

Write a cold email to a recruiter or HR manager about a job opportunity: RECRUITER'S NAME: [Name] COMPANY: [Company Name] ROLE I'M TARGETING: [Job Title — may or may not be currently listed] MY RELEVANT BACKGROUND: [3-4 line summary of my experience + key achievement] WHY THIS COMPANY: [genuine reason — product, culture, mission, recent news] REFERRAL/CONNECTION: [if any — "referred by [Name]" or "saw your post on LinkedIn"] Write: 1. SUBJECT LINE: 5 options (one name-drop, one achievement-led, one question-based, one direct, one curiosity-driven) 2. EMAIL BODY (under 150 words): - Opening: Reference something specific (their LinkedIn post, company news, or a mutual connection) - Value paragraph: Your top 2 achievements relevant to their needs (with numbers) - Ask: Simple, low-friction CTA ("Would you be open to a brief 10-minute call?") - Sign-off: Professional, warm 3. FOLLOW-UP EMAIL (to send if no reply in 5 days — under 80 words): - Brief, adds new value (share a relevant article or insight) - Restate your ask softly Rules: - Never sound needy ("I desperately need this job" = delete) - Position yourself as someone who adds value, not needs a favor - Keep the email scannable on a phone (short paragraphs, bullet points) - Don't attach resume in cold emails — wait for them to ask
💡 Pro Tip: Subject line decides if your email is opened. In India, "Referred by [Mutual Connection]" is the highest-opening subject line. If you don't have a referral, use "[Specific Achievement] — Interested in [Role] at [Company]". Avoid "Job Application for...".
9

Cold Email for Freelance/Contract Work

Write a cold email to pitch my freelance services: MY SERVICE: [what you offer — web development, content writing, design, marketing, etc.] TARGET CLIENT TYPE: [startups / agencies / SMBs / specific industry] CLIENT'S COMPANY: [their company name] PROBLEM I NOTICED: [a specific issue with their website/content/social media that I can fix] MY RELEVANT WORK: [1-2 relevant portfolio pieces or results] MY PRICE RANGE: [hourly / project-based — ₹ amount] Write: 1. SUBJECT LINE: 3 options (problem-focused, not "freelancer available") 2. EMAIL (under 120 words): - Line 1: Specific observation about THEIR business (shows you did research) - Line 2-3: The problem you identified and how it's costing them - Line 4-5: Your solution + 1 proof point (result you achieved for a similar client) - CTA: "Would a 15-minute call to discuss this make sense?" 3. PS LINE: Link to one relevant work sample Rules: - Lead with THEIR problem, not your skills - Never say "I am a freelancer looking for work" - One email = one problem = one service (don't pitch everything) - Include a specific result ("increased their traffic by 180%"), not vague claims
💡 Pro Tip: The "Problem I Noticed" is the key differentiator. Before emailing, spend 5 minutes analyzing their website. Screenshot a specific issue (slow load speed, poor SEO, outdated design). Attach the screenshot. This alone 5x your reply rate.
10

Follow-Up Email After Interview (Thank You Note)

Write a post-interview thank you email: INTERVIEWER'S NAME: [Name] THEIR ROLE: [e.g., Engineering Manager / VP of Marketing] COMPANY: [Company Name] ROLE INTERVIEWED FOR: [Job Title] INTERVIEW DATE: [when] KEY DISCUSSION POINTS: [what was discussed — specific projects, challenges, team structure] SOMETHING SPECIFIC THEY MENTIONED: [a challenge, project, or goal they shared during the interview] SOMETHING I WISH I'D SAID BETTER: [a question you fumbled or a point you want to reinforce] Write: 1. SUBJECT LINE: "Thank you — [specific reference to conversation]" 2. EMAIL (under 150 words): - Paragraph 1: Genuine thank you + reference a specific conversation moment - Paragraph 2: Reinforce your value — address the thing you wish you'd said better, or expand on a topic they cared about - Paragraph 3: Express enthusiasm + restate interest clearly - Close: Professional sign-off with timeline expectation Send within 4 hours of the interview. This email should NOT be generic — it must reference specific conversation details.
💡 Pro Tip: Only 24% of Indian candidates send thank-you emails. This alone puts you in the top quartile. The magic is in Paragraph 2 — use it to address any concern the interviewer had or strengthen a weak answer you gave during the interview.

🎤 Interview Preparation

11

STAR Method Interview Answer Generator

Help me prepare STAR method answers for behavioral interview questions: MY ROLE: [current/recent job title] COMPANY I'M INTERVIEWING AT: [Company Name] ROLE I'M INTERVIEWING FOR: [Target Job Title] MY RAW EXPERIENCES (I'll provide brief descriptions, you'll structure them): Experience 1: [e.g., "Led a project that was behind deadline and got it delivered"] Experience 2: [e.g., "Had a conflict with a teammate and resolved it"] Experience 3: [e.g., "Took initiative to automate a manual process"] Experience 4: [e.g., "Handled a difficult client who was unhappy"] Experience 5: [e.g., "Failed at something and learned from it"] For EACH experience, create a polished STAR answer: S — SITUATION: Set the scene (company, team, context) in 2 sentences T — TASK: What was your specific responsibility? 1 sentence A — ACTION: What exactly did YOU do? (3-4 specific actions — use "I", not "we") R — RESULT: Quantified outcome + what you learned. Include numbers. Then map each answer to common interview questions it can be used for: - "Tell me about a time you faced a challenge" - "Describe a situation where you showed leadership" - "Give an example of a time you failed" - "How do you handle conflicts at work?" - "Tell me about a time you went above and beyond" Each answer should be deliverable in under 2 minutes when spoken aloud.
💡 Pro Tip: Indian interviewers love the STAR method but most candidates ramble. Practice speaking each answer out loud with a timer — aim for 90-120 seconds. If it takes longer, cut the Situation section (most people over-explain context).
12

Company Research Cheat Sheet

Create a comprehensive pre-interview research cheat sheet about this company: COMPANY: [Company Name] ROLE I'M APPLYING FOR: [Job Title] Research and compile: 1. COMPANY OVERVIEW: What they do, founding year, headquarters, key products/services 2. RECENT NEWS: 3-5 recent developments (funding, launches, expansions, leadership changes) 3. COMPANY CULTURE: Values, work culture reputation (from Glassdoor/AmbitionBox insights) 4. COMPETITORS: Top 3 competitors and how this company differentiates 5. LEADERSHIP: CEO and relevant department heads (names, backgrounds) 6. INDIA OPERATIONS: Office locations, team size in India, India-specific initiatives 7. FINANCIAL HEALTH: Revenue stage, funding (if startup), public financials (if listed) 8. INTERVIEW INSIGHTS: Common interview questions reported for this company (from Glassdoor/AmbitionBox) 9. CHALLENGES/OPPORTUNITIES: What industry challenges the company faces 10. QUESTIONS I SHOULD ASK: 5 intelligent questions that show I've done my research Organize this as a 1-page quick-reference I can review 30 minutes before my interview.
💡 Pro Tip: The "Questions I Should Ask" section is a game-changer. Indian candidates often say "No questions, sir" when asked — this is a HUGE red flag. Always ask 2-3 questions. "What does success look like in this role in the first 90 days?" is universally impressive.
13

Technical Interview Prep (IT/Engineering)

Help me prepare for a technical interview: ROLE: [e.g., Frontend Developer / Data Engineer / Full-Stack / ML Engineer] COMPANY: [Company Name] TECH STACK IN JD: [e.g., React, Node.js, AWS / Python, SQL, Spark / Java, Spring Boot] INTERVIEW ROUND: [e.g., DSA coding round / system design / technical discussion / manager round] MY EXPERIENCE LEVEL: [years + primary tech stack] Generate: 1. TOP 15 LIKELY QUESTIONS: Based on the company's known interview pattern and the tech stack 2. For each question: - A clear, structured answer framework - Key terms/concepts to mention - A follow-up question they might ask + how to handle it 3. SYSTEM DESIGN SCENARIO (if applicable): A probable system design question + step-by-step approach 4. CODING TOPICS TO REVISE: Top 10 DSA topics with 2 practice problems each 5. "TELL ME ABOUT YOUR PROJECT" FRAMEWORK: How to present your best technical project in 3 minutes 6. RED FLAGS TO AVOID: Common mistakes Indian candidates make in tech interviews
💡 Pro Tip: For Indian product companies (Flipkart, PhonePe, Razorpay), system design questions are becoming more important than DSA for 3+ years experience. Practice designing systems like: "Design Razorpay's payment page" or "Design Swiggy's order tracking."
14

"Tell Me About Yourself" Script Generator

Write a compelling "Tell me about yourself" answer: MY BACKGROUND: [education, key career moves] MY CURRENT ROLE: [what you're doing now] MY KEY ACHIEVEMENT: [your proudest professional moment with numbers] ROLE I'M INTERVIEWING FOR: [target role] WHY I'M MAKING THIS MOVE: [genuine reason — growth, new challenge, industry shift] Write the answer using the PAST → PRESENT → FUTURE formula: PAST (20 sec): Brief background — where you started, 1-2 key career highlights PRESENT (20 sec): What you're currently doing + your biggest recent achievement FUTURE (20 sec): Why you're excited about THIS role + what you want to achieve next Rules: - Under 90 seconds when spoken aloud - NO chronological life story starting from "I was born in..." - Start with your most impressive achievement, not your college name - End with a natural transition to why this role excites you - Sound conversational, not rehearsed — but practiced Also provide: - 2 alternative openings (one for formal interviews, one for casual/startup) - Adjustments for fresher vs experienced versions
💡 Pro Tip: This is the FIRST question in 90% of Indian interviews. Your answer sets the tone for the entire interview. Record yourself saying it and listen back — if you say "um" more than twice or go over 90 seconds, practice more.

💰 Salary Negotiation

15

Salary Negotiation Email Template

Write a salary negotiation email after receiving a job offer: OFFER RECEIVED: ₹[CTC offered per annum] MY EXPECTED CTC: ₹[what I want] MY CURRENT CTC: ₹[current salary] ROLE OFFERED: [Job Title] COMPANY: [Company Name] MY LEVERAGE: [other offers / specialized skills / strong interview performance / rare experience] THEIR URGENCY: [how urgently do they need to fill this role] Write the email with: 1. OPENING: Express genuine gratitude and enthusiasm for the role (not fake) 2. CONTEXT: Explain why you're negotiating — reference market data, your current compensation, and the value you bring 3. YOUR ASK: State your expected CTC clearly and professionally 4. JUSTIFICATION: 3 specific reasons why this number is fair (your skills, market rate, value you'll add) 5. FLEXIBILITY: Show you're open to discussion (not an ultimatum) 6. ALTERNATIVES: If they can't match CTC, suggest alternatives (joining bonus, higher variable, ESOPs, remote work days, review in 6 months) 7. CLOSE: Restate excitement + ask for a call to discuss Rules: - Never reveal your current CTC first if you can avoid it (use "My expectation based on market research is...") - Never say "I need this salary because of personal expenses" — focus on VALUE you bring - Be confident, not arrogant - Under 200 words
💡 Pro Tip: In India, companies expect you to negotiate — NOT negotiating can actually signal low confidence. Always counter the first offer. A well-crafted negotiation email typically results in 10-20% uplift. The worst they can say is "this is our best offer."
16

Salary Research Script

Help me research what I should be earning: MY ROLE: [Job Title] MY EXPERIENCE: [years] MY LOCATION: [City] MY SKILLS: [key skills] MY CURRENT CTC: ₹[current package] COMPANY TYPE I'M TARGETING: [startup / MNC / product company / service company / Big 4] Generate: 1. MARKET SALARY RANGE: Expected CTC range for my profile (cite common India salary benchmarks) 2. FACTORS THAT INCREASE MY VALUE: Which of my skills command premium pricing 3. COMPANY TYPE COMPARISON: How salary differs between startups, product companies, and service companies for this role 4. CITY ADJUSTMENT: How my location affects the range 5. NEGOTIATION TALKING POINTS: 3 data-backed arguments I can use when asked "What's your expected CTC?" 6. TOTAL COMPENSATION CHECKLIST: Beyond CTC — what else to negotiate (ESOPs, joining bonus, remote flexibility, learning budget, relocation allowance) 7. RED FLAGS: Signs of lowball offers to watch for Reference: AmbitionBox, Glassdoor India, LinkedIn Salary Insights, Levels.fyi (for tech roles)
💡 Pro Tip: Never accept the first number. Always say "I'd like to understand the complete compensation structure" before discussing numbers. In India, the "in-hand" vs "CTC" difference can be 20-30% — always negotiate on in-hand take-home, not just CTC.

🔗 Advanced Workflow Chains

C1

Complete Job Application Chain (5 Steps)

Run each step in order. Feed each output into the next prompt. STEP 1 — Job Analysis: "Here's a job description I want to apply to: [paste full JD]. Analyze it completely: extract the top 15 keywords, identify the 5 must-have skills vs nice-to-have skills, determine the seniority level they're looking for, and identify what kind of candidate would be their dream hire." STEP 2 — Resume Tailoring: "Based on this analysis, here's my resume: [paste resume]. Rewrite my resume to be a 90%+ ATS match for this specific role. Use the extracted keywords naturally, rewrite bullets using XYZ formula, and prioritize the experiences most relevant to this JD." STEP 3 — Cover Letter: "Now write a cover letter for this application using the tailored resume. Reference something specific about the company, connect my top 2 achievements to their requirements, and end with a confident CTA. Under 250 words." STEP 4 — LinkedIn Optimization: "Update my LinkedIn headline and about section to align with this target role. Also write a connection request message for the hiring manager and a follow-up message." STEP 5 — Interview Prep: "Based on the job description and my tailored resume, generate: the top 10 interview questions I should prepare for, a 'Tell me about yourself' answer, and 3 intelligent questions I should ask the interviewer."
💡 Pro Tip: This 5-step chain is your complete job application system. For every job you're serious about, run this chain. It takes 30 minutes instead of 3 hours — and produces significantly better results than manual effort.
C2

Career Pivot Strategy Chain (3 Steps)

STEP 1 — Skills Audit: "I'm currently a [current role] and I want to transition to [target role]. My current skills are: [list all skills]. Analyze: which of my current skills transfer directly to the target role, which skills I need to learn, and what's the most efficient learning path to close the gap in 3-6 months." STEP 2 — Positioning Strategy: "Based on this skills audit, help me position my career pivot. Rewrite my professional narrative so that my career transition looks intentional, not random. Write: a new LinkedIn headline, an 'About' section that bridges both roles, and a 1-paragraph pitch for interviews explaining why I'm switching." STEP 3 — Action Plan: "Create a week-by-week 90-day action plan for my career pivot. Include: skills to learn (with specific free/paid Indian courses), projects to build for portfolio, people to network with (by role/company type), content to post on LinkedIn for visibility, and a job application strategy."
💡 Pro Tip: Career pivots in India are increasingly common and accepted — especially into product management, data science, and digital marketing from engineering. The key is positioning: don't apologize for switching, show how your previous experience is a UNIQUE advantage.

⚡ Quick-Fire Prompts

Q1

Rejection Response Email

"I just received a rejection email from [Company] for the [Role]. Write a graceful response that: thanks them for the opportunity, expresses continued interest in future roles, asks for specific feedback on my application, and leaves the door open for reconnection. Keep it under 80 words. Professional but warm."
Q2

Resignation Email

"Write a professional resignation email. I'm leaving [Current Company] as [Role]. My notice period is [X weeks/months]. I want to leave on positive terms — thank my manager, offer to help with transition, and keep it brief. Last working day: [Date]. Tone: grateful, professional, no bridges burned."
Q3

Freelancer Rate Card Writer

"I'm a freelance [skill] in India. Create a professional rate card for my services. My services include: [list 4-6 services]. Create 3 pricing tiers (Starter, Pro, Premium) with: tier name, what's included, price in ₹, ideal client type, and turnaround time. Also suggest an hourly rate range for custom projects."
Q4

Portfolio Project Description

"I have this project: [project name + brief description of what you built]. Tech stack: [technologies used]. Write a portfolio description that includes: 1 compelling headline, a 100-word project overview using non-technical language, 'My Role' section, 'Key Challenges & How I Solved Them' (3 bullet points), and 'Results/Impact'. Make it sound impressive to a non-technical hiring manager."
Q5

Upwork/Freelancer Profile Optimizer

"Optimize my Upwork profile. I offer [services] and target [client type]. My experience: [brief background]. Write: 1) A profile title (under 70 characters) that makes me stand out from thousands of Indian freelancers, 2) A profile overview (under 500 words) that: opens with a bold result, lists my expertise with proof, addresses client objections, and ends with a CTA. Make me sound like an expert, not a cheap option."
